user_questions.question: Q1: Who records a partial redemption, and where? (a) internal staff in the Salesforce UI on the certificate [recommended; nothing in the org records redemptions today]; (b) an Agentforce agent action; (c) an external POS/storefront system via API. Q2: Should the Case link be enforced for service-recovery certificates? (a) make it possible on every issuance path by adding an optional caseId to IssueGiftCardAction, no hard rule [recommended]; (b) also require Issued_For_Case__c when Type__c = Recovery via validation rule (the existing Issue_Gift_Card agent action would then fail when no case is passed).
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Step 5 lists 'which channel/persona' as an intent question, but when the hidden intent is terse the only answer is 'no preference', so asking produced no information; the skill gives no guidance on skipping the question when the recommended default is clearly safe.

The I template has no slot for the validation-rule-on-update edge case; AskCoworker's child-level 'Amount__c > parent Remaining_Value__c' rule was wrong on edits and bulk, and correcting it required redesigning rows myself. The Rule 'Correct rows the facts contradict' covers facts, not flawed logic; it is unclear whether a logic redesign should trigger a resend of I (counts as follow-up) or be done locally.

AskCoworker repeatedly labeled facts '[Verified: prior session]' that I had sent it; the skill's memory rule says echoed facts are established, but it also cited a DataStream count I had not sent, which needed a separate check.

R call with the full 14-row inventory timed out at 60s even at 400 words; the template's accepted-inventory list plus the Established block is too long for R on medium inventories. The narrower retry dropped permission/CRUD topics, which then had to be covered from org queries alone; the skill does not say whether a split R counts as covering the whole topic.
org-verification.md suggests ValidationRule via Tooling but does not warn that ErrorConditionFormula is not selectable in a multi-row query (it is a Metadata-only field), costing one failed query.

spec-format says 'For flow-only changes, use Flow Tests', but for a record-triggered flow driven by roll-up recalculation an Apex DML test is the natural choice; the rule's boundary (flow-only vs. mixed inventory) is ambiguous.
